$comment: A staleness budget for the documents whose age costs something.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `npm run docs:parity` holds the bilingual pair in step, `npm run
adr:check` fails an ADR citing a path that has been renamed, and `test-unit/docs-task-index.test.mjs`
fails a route into a file that has moved. Every one of those checks INTERNAL consistency —
so parity is checked but age is not, and the failure mode they all leave open is a page
that is perfectly consistent, routed to correctly, spelled the same in both languages, and
describing a seam that moved six months ago. Nothing goes red for that, and on a repository
where an agent orients from documents before it reads code, a confidently wrong page is worse
than a missing one.
WHAT IS MEASURED. For each entry, `npm run docs:staleness` asks git two questions: when was
the DOC last touched, and when was the newest commit to any path in `watches`. A doc is stale
when the code it describes has moved since the doc was last read (`overtakenBy`), or when the
doc itself has gone longer than `maxAgeDays` without anyone looking at it. Age is measured in
COMMITS TO THE THINGS THE DOC NAMES rather than in days alone, because a runbook for a seam
nobody has touched in a year is not stale — it is finished.
RUNG (docs/adr/0007-gate-rung-discipline.md). `ratchet.stale` is null, which means nobody has
measured this yet, so `--check` REPORTS and exits 0. That is the honest rung for a check whose
baseline is unknown: ADR-0007 says a gate blocks only once it passes. One run closes it:
npm run docs:staleness                      # see the number
npm run docs:staleness -- --accept --reason "..."   # pin it; the count may never rise
After that a doc going stale fails `npm run docs:staleness:check`, and the way back is to read
the doc — not to raise the ratchet.
WHAT IS BLOCKING TODAY: test-unit/docs-staleness.test.mjs, inside `npm run test:unit` inside
`check:ci`. It fails when an entry names a document or a watched path that does not exist, and
when a runbook lands in docs/runbooks/ with no budget — so the registry cannot quietly stop
covering the documents it was written for.
NOT GOVERNED, ON PURPOSE: the ADRs themselves. A decision record describes the decision as it
was made; it ages into history rather than into error, and `npm run adr:check` already fails
one whose cited paths have moved. The scan reports (docs/harness/**) are dated artefacts of a
run and are the same case.

docs.why: The first page anyone opens, and the source edition of the bilingual pair.
Transcreated from README.md. docs:parity holds the declared claims; nothing holds the rest of the page.
The cloud-connected walkthrough. Already known to be partly stale — it predates the offline path, and the task index says so.
It says the same things as AGENTS.md to a human. When AGENTS.md moves and this does not, a contributor is told the old rules.
A routing table read at the start of a run. Its links are asserted; whether its ROUTES still describe the tree is not.
The other start-of-run lookup — which subagent to hand a task to.
The runbook for env names, crons and rollback. A wrong page here is read during an incident.
The way back out. A runbook that no longer matches its script is found out at the worst moment.

The way a credential is taken away. It is the one procedure here that is performed under real time pressure, and it is read by somebody who has already lost control of a value — so a page describing a crypto seam that has since moved does not merely misinform, it sends them to re-key against the wrong file. Watched against the threat model in particular, because that is where the fifteenth credential arrives in a table of fourteen.
Tokens and the shared primitives every new component inherits.
The colocated-dictionary contract. Which locale is the source has already flipped once.
Describes a benchmark that costs money to run; a stale description is an expensive wrong expectation.
The lead entity layer's design record, and the layer is under active change.
Read by someone outside this repository, who cannot check it against the code.
How a stopped run hands off. Read by an agent that is already in trouble.

The record of what agents got wrong here, and the standing of each trap — whether a fence now refuses it, or nothing does. When the guidance surface moves under it, a row that says 'nothing catches this' may have become false, or a fence it names may have gone; both read as evidence and neither would be noticed otherwise.

Where every credential enters, rests and leaves, mapped to the fence standing on each edge. It is the page a contributor reads BEFORE touching a key path, so a stale row does not misinform them about the seam — it tells them a fence exists where one has been removed.
